title: Abstract window and reflection deductions
assumption: The stated window and reflection premises.
conclusion: Zero exclusion and the critical-line deduction for abstract predicates.

declarations.name: Reading.excludeZeroByWindows
declarations.assumption: Arbitrarily late good windows exist, a zero makes every late window bad, and good and bad are incompatible.
declarations.conclusion: The zero is excluded.

declarations.name: Reading.criticalLineByReflection
declarations.assumption: Trichotomy, reflection of left-hand zeros, and exclusion on the right.
declarations.conclusion: Every zero lies on the designated line.

title: Integer-sphere proof
assumption: Integer vectors in one finite dimension have the same squared norm. Their relation is j(v−u)=i(w−u), with j≠0 and i≠j.
conclusion: Positive squared distance, the chord identity, and exclusion of three distinct collinear lattice points.

declarations.name: BehrendReading.normSq_nonneg
declarations.assumption: Any integer vector in finite dimension.
declarations.conclusion: Its sum of coordinate squares is nonnegative.

declarations.name: BehrendReading.coordinates_zero_of_normSq_zero
declarations.assumption: Its squared norm equals zero.
declarations.conclusion: Every coordinate is zero.

declarations.name: BehrendReading.distance_pos_of_ne
declarations.assumption: Two finite-dimensional integer vectors differ.
declarations.conclusion: Their squared distance is positive.

declarations.name: BehrendReading.chord_identity
declarations.assumption: j(v−u)=i(w−u) coordinatewise.
declarations.conclusion: j(j−i)Q(v−u)=i²(Q(w)−Q(u))−ij(Q(v)−Q(u)), where Q is squared norm.

declarations.name: BehrendReading.sphere_rel
declarations.assumption: Integer vectors in one finite dimension have the same squared norm. Their relation is j(v−u)=i(w−u), with j≠0 and i≠j.
declarations.conclusion: The second vector equals the first.

declarations.name: BehrendReading.sphere_midpoint
declarations.assumption: Integer vectors in one finite dimension have the same squared norm. Also 2v=u+w.
declarations.conclusion: All three points coincide.

title: Closing deductions
assumption: Right-half-plane nonvanishing of zeta or of all Dirichlet L-functions, as specified.
conclusion: The corresponding zeta RH or all-character strip statement follows.

declarations.name: Claim.strip
declarations.assumption: Every Dirichlet character has a nonzero L-function for Re(s)>½, with the principal pole excluded.
declarations.conclusion: Every zero of any Dirichlet character in 0<Re(s)<1 has real part ½.

declarations.name: Claim.zeta
declarations.assumption: Every Dirichlet character has a nonzero L-function for Re(s)>½, with the principal pole excluded.
declarations.conclusion: Every zeta zero away from the trivial zeros and the pole has real part ½.

declarations.name: Formalism.VW.rh_of_right
declarations.assumption: Zeta has no zero for Re(s)>½ away from s=1.
declarations.conclusion: Mathlib’s RiemannHypothesis follows.

title: Analytic and Behrend landmarks
assumption: Separate hypotheses for each selected result, given in the theorem table.
conclusion: Pole data for finite character families and a zero-free criterion from a uniform window bound. Relation avoidance on digit spheres and a quantitative large-set construction.

declarations.name: Deduction.zeroFree_of_rpow_window
declarations.assumption: Fix a finite admissible positively weighted character family, 0<θ<1 and δ>0. A single C bounds its centered sum by C·y^θ throughout arbitrarily late [Y,Y^(1+δ)].
declarations.conclusion: Every L-function in the family is nonzero for Re(s)>θ.

declarations.name: Deduction.poleData
declarations.assumption: A finite admissible character family with positive weights.
declarations.conclusion: Its logarithmic prime-sum transform has the stated Laplace representation and a simple pole with nonzero residue at each marked zero.

declarations.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.ThickExists.sphere_rel
declarations.assumption: Integer vectors in one finite dimension have the same squared norm. Their relation is j(v−u)=i(w−u), with j≠0 and i≠j.
declarations.conclusion: The two indicated vectors coincide in the archive’s finite-sum normalization.

declarations.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.ThickExists.noRel_image
declarations.assumption: Base 4Ld encoding of a digit sphere, L≥1.
declarations.conclusion: Three distinct encoded elements avoid j(s₂−s₁)=i(s₃−s₁) for distinct nonzero coefficients bounded by L in absolute value.

declarations.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.hostThickExists
declarations.assumption: Natural n and L with L≥2.
declarations.conclusion: One absolute C supplies a set of size at least (n/L)exp(−C√(log n·log L)), with 4Ls<n for each s and the stated relation avoidance.

authority: Reading proof using the original archive

title: Finite character balance and prime windows
assumption: The source's character estimates, size and norm inequalities, and compatible hosts on the window.
conclusion: Four deductions transfer the theta discrepancy to a weighted prime-sum upper bound with an explicit exponent.

declarations.name: Deduction.ch_top
declarations.assumption: At one scale, the finite theta data satisfy the main-term identification, size, error, norm and large-x bounds.
declarations.conclusion: Each host row's discrepancy is bounded by the explicit error bracket times x^(CErr·ε).

declarations.name: Deduction.ch_core
declarations.assumption: The finite group and characters obey the stated host, size, density and cost conditions, and every row in the subgroup satisfies the discrepancy bound.
declarations.conclusion: The retained prime sum is at most x^(½+(C+3)ε) plus the discarded-character contribution.

declarations.name: UpperTheory.Comparison₂.core_gm
declarations.assumption: Fix the level, constants and ε>0. At each sufficiently large x assume EAtH and CoreAtH for the same frame, host and set of classes.
declarations.conclusion: The weighted level sum is at most x^(½+(eD+eL+7)ε).

declarations.name: UpperTheory.Comparison₂.windowInequality_of_artinInputs
declarations.assumption: Tied data for a family and scale supply at least one controlled host there.
declarations.conclusion: The uniform Chebyshev inequality holds at each sufficiently large scale of the specified windows, subject to the level and tie conditions.

title: The mathematical language of the five endpoints

conclusion: Five statement equivalences and a concrete level-two boundary zero.
authority: Reading proof using the original archive

declarations.name: Reading.Reference.mathlib_iff_reference

declarations.conclusion: Mathlib’s RH and the reference are logically equivalent.

declarations.name: Reading.Reference.zeta_iff_reference
declarations.assumption: The explicit archived zeta zero statement.
declarations.conclusion: Its exclusion of the negative even integers is equivalent to excluding −2k for every positive natural k.

declarations.name: Reading.Reference.right_iff_reference

declarations.name: Reading.Reference.strip_iff_reference

declarations.conclusion: It quantifies equivalently over every level m+1 and the open strip 0<Re(s)<1.
declarations.authority: Reading proof using the original archive

declarations.name: Reading.Reference.primitive_iff_reference
declarations.assumption: The archive’s primitive-character zero assertion.
declarations.conclusion: It is equivalent to the positive-level statement with primitivity and both open-strip inequalities imposed together.

declarations.name: Reading.Reference.boundary_example

title: The arithmetic source of the windows
assumption: Assume TopG and VWinAt ψ 401 for the prescribed primitive character.
conclusion: The cyclic family's sum is at most y^θ on whole late windows. For the character modulo one this sum equals G(y).

declarations.name: Reading.ArithmeticWindows.level_windows
declarations.assumption: Fix a primitive character ψ. Assume TopG and VWinAt ψ 401 and take θ>½.
declarations.conclusion: On arbitrarily late intervals [Y,Y^(3/2)], the centered sum of ψ’s cyclic family is at most y^θ for every y in the interval.

declarations.name: Reading.ArithmeticWindows.trivial_level_eq

declarations.name: Reading.ArithmeticWindows.zeta_windows

title: The converse for the ordinary zeta window
